---
description: Classify reviewed requirements and author native feature specs.
agent: agent
---

Require one explicit GitHub Feature issue reference in the invocation, either
an issue number such as `#8` or the issue URL. If it is missing, stop
immediately and ask the Business Analyst to provide the Feature issue number.
Do not search for, list, infer, or select an issue from repository state,
conversation history, recent activity, or open issues.

Verify that the supplied issue exists, has the `feature` label, identifies one
reviewed Requirement increment, and is activated at `Ready / Ready for
Refinement`. If any condition fails, stop and tell the Business Analyst what
must be corrected.

Use only reviewed intake-scoped requirements and recorded human decisions.
Read their `requirement_group` values and registries as contextual navigation,
but derive epic and feature boundaries independently. A feature may contain
REQs from multiple intake groups, and one group may feed multiple features.
Never treat a group as a required epic or feature boundary.
Invoke the feature skills in project routing order:
`requirement-refinement`, `open-question-handling`, `gherkin-authoring`,
`feature-grouping`, and `spec-compilation`.

Select exactly one mode.

## Prepare mode

Use this mode when `--submit` is absent. Build repository context before
changing feature membership. Propose one of `extend-existing`, `create-new`,
`split-requirement`, or `needs-clarification`, with supporting evidence,
alternatives, build implications, proposed epic and feature boundaries, REQ
membership, dependencies, and how the proposed boundary intentionally relates
to—but is not dictated by—the intake groups.

Present the proposal for human review and always provide a `Provide a different
classification` option. Allow the human to move REQs, split or combine proposed
features, select another classification, or provide a custom classification.
For custom input, explain its implications, present the revised complete
grouping, and request final confirmation. Do not update feature membership,
allocate IDs, or create a workspace before explicit human confirmation.

If the confirmed classification is `needs-clarification`, or any blocking
ambiguity is found while authoring, invoke `open-question-handling`. Present
exactly one question at a time with existing options, implications, and a
`Provide a different decision` choice. Record only explicit human decisions
with the named decider and ISO date. Stop if the human stops or any blocking
question remains, then reconfirm classification after the decisions.

After confirmation, create or update `specs/_index/features.md`, stamp `feature`,
`epic`, and acyclic `depends_on` membership on every in-scope REQ, and ensure
there are no orphan REQs or features. Create or update the persistent
`specs/<sequence>-<feature-slug>/spec.md` workspaces with status `draft`.
Author solution-agnostic intent, scope, actors, functional behaviour, UX
behaviour, happy/negative/boundary scenarios, NFRs, dependencies, open
questions, and traceability. Do not select D365, Dataverse, Power Platform,
Azure, or implementation components.

Run `python scripts/compile_repository_context.py`,
`python scripts/compile_specs.py`, `python scripts/compile_specs.py --check`,
`python scripts/validate_reqs.py`, and `python scripts/validate_specs.py`.
Do not compile or modify `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, or DEV artifacts during the
Feature stage. Stop for Business Analyst and Product/Customer review without
committing or opening a pull request.

After presenting the classification, authored workspace, coverage, open
question, and validation summary, stop with the files uncommitted for human
review. Do not ask whether to submit, do not mark specs as `reviewed`, and do
not continue into Submit mode. Submission requires a later explicit
`/d365.specify #<issue-number> --submit` invocation.

## Submit mode

Use this mode only when the invocation contains `--submit`. Treat the explicit
invocation as confirmation that the local Feature review is complete. If an
in-scope spec is still `draft`, change only that spec's status to `reviewed`;
never advance it to `approved`.

Resolve the confirmed classification and exact in-scope REQ and feature set
from the supplied issue. Do not reclassify, change feature boundaries, or
rewrite authored behaviour in Submit mode. Require every in-scope REQ to be
`reviewed`, every in-scope spec to be `reviewed`, bidirectional feature
membership to agree, dependencies to form a DAG, and all recorded questions to
be closed with a named human decider and ISO date.

Run `python scripts/compile_repository_context.py`,
`python scripts/compile_repository_context.py --check`,
`python scripts/compile_specs.py`, `python scripts/compile_specs.py --check`,
`python scripts/validate_reqs.py`, and `python scripts/validate_specs.py`. Stop
if classification is unconfirmed, membership is incomplete, any question
remains open, a generated projection is stale, or validation fails.

Create a focused branch and stage only the in-scope REQ files whose feature
metadata changed, `specs/_index/features.md`, the in-scope feature `spec.md`
files, `specs/_index/repository-context.json`, and
`.specify/context/spec-context.json`. Never stage raw intake documents,
`plan.md`, `tasks.md`, DEV artifacts, `audit/`, temporary files, or unrelated
changes. Check the staged diff before committing.

Commit, push, and open one pull request with the configured Feature title. Its
body must contain `Closes #<issue-number>`, the recorded classification,
epic/feature IDs, REQ membership and coverage, dependency summary, validation
results, clarification closure summary, and an unchecked Gate 2 checklist. If
an open pull request already exists for the same issue and feature set, report
it instead of creating a duplicate. Stop before approval or merge.
